A1.justification: Despite changes to the title, authors and method name, both PDFs describe the same program-learning work. All 32 pages of v1 and 31 pages of v2, including figures, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report original program-synthesis, neural-training, fine-tuning, in-context learning, generalization and ablation results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain original experiments and report additional algorithmic-task, baseline and tabular-benchmark results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 removes optional candidate batches and validation-threshold early stopping, instead sampling one candidate per trial and returning the best after k trials. The fixed-prompt proposal, execution and validation-selection mechanism remains; renaming LLM-ERM to LLM-PV is not itself a method change.

E1.justification: v2 adds shifted primality (IsPrime+47), graph cycle density, and five tabular benchmarks: Adult Income, Secondary Mushroom, CDC Diabetes Health Indicators, HRTU2 and Chess. Unrestricted primality evaluation disappears, while v1's restricted-last-digit variant is retained under the shorter name IsPrime.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds evaluated XGBoost, Random Forest, SVM, genetic-programming and TabPFN comparators. Table 4 additionally includes Decision Tree. Fine-tuned models also enter the length-generalization and data-scaling comparisons in Figures 3–4, which previously compared the proposed method with training from scratch.

E3.justification: Fine-tuning hyperparameter selection changes from best training accuracy in v1 Appendix A.2.2 to best test performance in v2 Appendix A.2; Table 2 reports maxima across models and configurations. New tabular experiments specify fixed 100/100 training/validation samples, original test sets and random diagonal affine preprocessing. The selection-text revision does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a shifted-primality diagnostic addressing reliance on superficial primality cues and extends length/data-scaling analyses to fine-tuned comparators. Figure 1 replaces the earlier 50-digit primality case with a 100-digit reasoning trace. Most existing scaling and hyperparameter-analysis questions remain, although their reporting is condensed.

E5.justification: v2 Table 4 introduces accuracy estimates with ± terms, whereas v1 reports point accuracies. Their meaning and repeated-run counts are unspecified, so additional replication cannot be established. v1's explicit seed 42 disclosure for Random 10-Parity is also absent from v2.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive comparator and tabular results, including 80.6% on IsPrime+47 and 96.9% on CycleCount at n=100. Reported Dyck-2 accuracy at n=100 changes from 80.1% in v1 Table 1 to 100% in v2 Tables 1–2. Numerous individual configuration results disappear into maxima. Conflicting Pattern1/Pattern2 labels prevent clean attribution of some transferred scores.

T1.justification: v1's general SQ-dimension bound T = Omega(d epsilon^2/B^(3/2)) is replaced by a planted-k-parity bound TB = Omega(sqrt(binomial(n,k))/2^b) under explicit b-bit coordinate-gradient access. v2 also adds a quantization-stability lemma, revised statistical-dimension derivations, and a proposal-mass-dependent validation generalization theorem with proof. The program-enumeration bound is retained.

C1.justification: The central theoretical contribution narrows from general SQ-dimension SGD hardness to finite-precision coordinate SGD on planted parity. The introduction explicitly disclaims new PAC/SQ machinery or constraint solvers and positions the contribution as an LLM proposal prior for synthesis and ERM. Main empirical comparisons also expand to classical learners.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the method discussion's adaptive-search explanation with a proposal-prior account whose effectiveness depends on the probability of sampling a good program. It adds interpretations of shifted-primality performance and tabular applicability. It also qualifies the large-data CAP failure to n>=25, acknowledging the short-length success already visible in v1's results.

D1.justification: v2 adds classical-baseline hyperparameter grids, genetic-programming operators and budgets, graph-generation/tokenization details, and tabular preprocessing instructions. The code link points to LLM_PV instead of LLM_ERM. Conversely, v1's two-H100 hardware disclosure and detailed Qwen architecture dimensions are removed. Most existing neural-training and GPT-5 decoding settings are retained.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands into programming by examples, enumerative synthesis, version spaces and CEGIS, with additions including Gulwani, Lau, Solar-Lezama, Jain, Li and Ellis, Khan, and CodeARC. The new 'Our lens' discussion explicitly derives the approach from synthesis/PBE and distinguishes distributional validation from consistency with a finite specification.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method narrative and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Related Work becomes a standalone section, experiments gain Setup/Methods Compared/Main Results subsections, and the appendices are reorganized into baseline details, condensed analyses and a separate finite-precision theory appendix. Title, terminology and author-list edits accompany this restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 substantially redesigns the presentation: expanded comparison matrices replace many plots and detailed tables, hyperparameter sweeps become a maxima table, reasoning traces are redrawn and consolidated, and the workflow diagram changes. Length/scaling figures gain comparator curves, and tabular results receive a new table. Replacing infinity-percent notation with 100-dagger preserves its stated meaning.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central argument: v1 offered ERM-style assurances without a method-specific bound and compared mainly with neural learners; v2 adds a conditional proposal/validation theorem, explicit finite-precision restrictions on SGD hardness, and direct classical/TabPFN comparisons. Broader empirical evaluation and PBE positioning improve support and clarify novelty. Conflicting pattern labels, test-based tuning and unexplained ± values remain material weaknesses, but the theoretical and comparative gains outweigh them.
